newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Thailand to help Malaysia curb illegal workers.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to help Malaysia curb illegal workers.

text.p: Thailand has pledged to help Malaysian authorities stem an influx of illegal Bangladeshi workers into Malaysia across the two countries' common border, the national Bernama news agency reported on Tuesday.
Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn made the pledge during talks with his Malaysian counterpart Abdullah Ahmad Badawi here on Tuesday.

The newly-appointed Thai minister, who is leading a 21-member delegation, arrived on Monday night for a three-day visit as part of a tour of Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member countries.

Malaysia is cracking down on its growing numbers of illegal workers and last week deported a group of 1,000 Indonesian workers who did not register for working papers under a three-month anmesty which ended on December 31, 1996.
About 700,000 workers are believed to have missed the deadline.
Prachuab told reporters that although not all Bangladeshi illegal workers entered Malaysia through the common border shared by the countries, Thailand would help regardless.
"Whatever it is, we are more than willing to give our cooperation in curbing this problem once and for all," Bernama quoted him as saying.
Prachuab said Bangladeshi workers enter Thailand with proper tourist visas but often elect to cross illegally into Malaysia without the necessary documents.
Thailand in late December cracked down on Bangladeshi and other workers illegally entering the country, saying that about 5,000 Bangladeshis were hiding in the jungles near Malaysia.
Abdullah said officials from both countries were expected to meet soon to discuss how best to stop the flow of illegal Bangladeshi workers before submitting proposals to their respective governments.
Abdullah said he also discussed with the Thai minister some unresolved problems pertaining to border demarcation along the common border.
